solution: Let $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=\frac1x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{x^{2}}{2}$. Then $\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^{2}}{2}\ln x-\int\frac{x^{2}}{2}\cdot\frac1x\,dx=\frac{x^{2}}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^{2}}{4}+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $\bigl[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigr]_{1}^{e}=\bigl(\frac{e^{2}}{2}-\frac{e^{2}}{4}\bigr)-\bigl(0-\frac{1}{4}\bigr)=\frac{e^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{e^{2}+1}{4}$.
hints: Choose u=ln x and dv=x dx.
Evaluate at the limits 1 and e.
